name: TAROK ROMANIAN
description: Romanian Tarok is a point-trick game played mainly around Suceava in Moldavia. Card values: skiz, luna, lowest trump and Kings 5, Queens 4, horses 3, Jacks 2, others 1. Objective: win tricks with valuable cards. Follow suit; must trump if unable. Introduced from Austria in the 19th century; played mainly around Suceava in Moldavia. 54-card Austrian tarok pack; point-trick with call a King; three-player Taper and other regional variants exist.
Four players (principal form); three-player variant Taper when a fourth is not available.
54-card Austrian tarok (22 trumps plus 8 cards in each of four suits: hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades).
Dealer places first 6 cards face down in the centre as the talon, then deals the remaining 48 cards in batches of 6 so each player receives 12 cards. Deal and play anticlockwise.

items.text: Taper (three players): Three-player form. 42-card pack (remove lowest three cards of each suit). No king called; declarer always plays alone against two in partnership. Twelve cards each, 6 to talon. Lowest bid unul de trei (take three from talon). Declarations 10, 11 or 12 taroace. No rege ultimo; no michi-michi (if all pass, cards thrown in and radler of three hands at double stakes).

Michi-michi: Played when all four players pass. Talon set aside; twelve tricks under usual rules but objective is to avoid winning tricks. No card points, declarations or bonuses. Each player pays one game point to the pool per trick won. Next four hands played at double stakes (radler).
